messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated error rate on hosted-prod: /v1/chat 5xx=13%, /v1/embeddings latency doubled, rerank timeouts increasing. Alert triggered 2026-03-16T21:08:42Z. Auto-page -> Alex.
Alex (oncall): taking this. Quick dashboard glance: large embedding batches plus a surge of synchronous rerank calls from an internal experiment bucket. Shared GPU pool saturation looks likely.
Pri (platform): I see high GPU queue depth and KV-cache churn. Top callers: data-sci-backfill and chat-loadtest. Preemption is slow.
Noor (runtime): quick mitigation levers: per-route qps/concurrency caps, per-tenant token budgets, rerank soft-disable (429), model fallback for chat, and routing embeddings to a standby pool. Suggest minimal-impact first: target heavy tenants.
Alex (oncall): agree. Jen, can you pull the top offending tenants and flag enterprise accounts?
Jen (support): on it. Top offenders: data-sci-backfill (huge embedding batches), chat-loadtest (internal), plus a smaller tenant "exp-rerank" doing aggressive rerank calls. Two enterprise tenants in region unaffected so far.
Alex (oncall): applying targeted per-tenant caps and a per-request embeddings ceiling. Commands: ```
# redwoodctl quota-bucket create --tenant data-sci-backfill --route embeddings --tokens 30000 --window 3600 --burst 1 --reason "live mitigation: large backfill"
# redwoodctl quota update --route embeddings --match "tenant:exp-rerank" --qps 0.05 --reason "mitigate heavy rerank->embeddings amplification"
# redwoodctl route-config set --route embeddings --cfg "max_tokens_per_request=12000" --reason "prevent oversized requests"
```
Pri (platform): rules accepted and propagated to gateways. I'm also recommending a rerank soft-disable for non-enterprise to avoid downstream amplification; that'll return 429+Retry-After.
Noor (runtime): applying rerank soft-disable for free/standard tiers now: ```
# redwoodctl route-toggle --route rerank --enable false --match "tier:free,tier:standard" --response 429 --reason "reduce backend amplification"
```
Alex (oncall): also limit chat concurrency for free tier to protect p95: ```
# redwoodctl quota update --route chat --match "tier:free" --concurrency 1 --reason "protect tail latency"
```
Carlos (cs): I'm notifying affected account owners for data-sci-backfill and exp-rerank. If enterprise customers get affected, I'll escalate.
Jen (support): queued tenant messages: "We've applied temporary per-endpoint rate limits and routing changes to restore service. If this blocks critical workflows let us know and we'll coordinate a controlled window." Sending after we confirm metrics.
Pri (platform): immediate telemetry: data-sci-backfill embeddings tokens/min dropped ~80% within 90s, chat 5xx down 13% -> 6% in same window. Good signal.
Noor (runtime): follow-ups: we can optionally route non-enterprise embeddings to standby-embeddings pool to permanently reduce shared-pool contention during the incident. Shall I shift?
Alex (oncall): yes but only for non-enterprise tenants. Execute routing override for those tiers.
Pri (platform): running routing change: ```
# redwoodctl routing override --route embeddings --match "tier:free,tier:standard" --to-pool standby-embeddings-3 --reason "offload non-enterprise embeddings during incident"
```
Pri (platform): override accepted. Standby pool picking up traffic; shared queue depth falling further.
Carlos (cs): contacted the two account owners; data-sci-backfill replied they will stagger jobs on their side. exp-rerank requests ETA for lift.
Alex (oncall): plan: keep per-tenant buckets and embeddings per-request ceiling for 30m. Keep rerank soft-disable for 45m. Slowly relax quotas for tenants with no regressions: 2x every 10m. Handoff in 20m to oncall-follow if stable.
oncall-follow: ack, I will take handoff.
Noor (runtime): adding a model-variant fallback for chat for non-paid tiers to reduce KV cache pressure; route chat-large -> chat-medium for matchers. Applying: ```
# redwoodctl routing override --route chat --match "tier:free,tier:standard" --model chat-medium --reason "temporary fallback to reduce KV churn"
```
Pri (platform): applied. After fallback and routing shifts, p95 improved ~30% and aggregated 5xx across routes at ~2.8% after 7 minutes.
Jen (support): sending tenant notices now. Two tickets opened and linked to this thread. No escalations at present.
Alex (oncall): documenting rollback snippets here in case metrics regress: ```
# redwoodctl quota-bucket delete --tenant data-sci-backfill --route embeddings --reason "rollback"
# redwoodctl quota update --route embeddings --match "tenant:exp-rerank" --qps 5 --reason "rollback"
# redwoodctl route-config set --route embeddings --cfg "max_tokens_per_request=65536" --reason "rollback"
# redwoodctl route-toggle --route rerank --enable true --match "tier:free,tier:standard" --reason "rollback"
# redwoodctl routing override --route chat --match "tier:free,tier:standard" --model chat-default --reason "rollback"
# redwoodctl routing override --route embeddings --match "tier:free,tier:standard" --to-pool shared-gpu-pool --reason "rollback"
```
Pri (platform): follow-ups I'll run: collect batcher histograms, inspect nvlink and driver logs on nodes that handled heavy load, and add an alert for per-tenant token/day spikes to catch large backfills earlier.
Alex (oncall): posting a targeted status to affected tenants now; holding a broad status until we confirm full recovery for 30m. I will hand primary to oncall-follow in 20m.
incident-bot: Incident page created -> https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2730001122
Alex (oncall): handing primary to oncall-follow for monitoring at 21:28 UTC. I am unassigning primary.
